samasa.sense: the spear that makes the life-breath depart — Yama’s weapon

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (राजन् becomes the a-stem राज at the end of a compound)
samasa.literal: of the king of the waters

morph.note: Genitive singular of the ṛ-stem भ्रातृ: -ṛ + -as → -uḥ (cf. पितुः, मातुः).
Feminine past participle of √हृ agreeing with शक्तिः, used with the agent instrumental त्वया as a passive past: ‘was taken by you’.

mantras.anvaya: ईश, मृत्योः उत्क्रान्तिदा नाम शक्तिः त्वया हृता; सलिलराजस्य पाशः तव भ्रातुः परिग्रहे (अस्ति)।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two clauses: a passive past (शक्तिः … त्वया हृता) and a nominal sentence of place with the copula understood (पाशः … परिग्रहे).
mantras.lit: The spear of Death named Utkrāntidā has been taken by you, O lord; the noose of the king of the waters is in your brother’s possession.
mantras.tr: ‘You have taken, lord, Death’s spear called Utkrāntidā; and the noose of Varuṇa, king of the waters, is held by your brother.’

comm.t: Now the weapons: Yama’s spear Utkrāntidā, ‘giver of the soul’s departure’, taken by Śumbha, and Varuṇa’s noose, held by Niśumbha. Śumbha and his brother between them hold the instruments of death and of binding.
Both seizures fill out the opening statement of the chapter, that the brothers took the offices of Yama (याम्यम्) and Varuṇa (वरुणस्य) (5.3).

samasa.sense: ocean-born gems (pearls, coral and the like)
samasa.alt: Also saptamī tatpuruṣa, अब्धौ जाताः ‘born in the ocean’; the sense is the same.

samasa.literal: (two garments) whose cleansing is by fire
samasa.sense: garments purified by fire, a mark of divine cloth

morph.note: Neuter dual of the s-stem वासस् ‘garment’: -as + -ī → -असी, ‘a pair of garments’ (upper and lower cloth).
Dative singular of युष्मद् — the full form, beside the enclitic ते used in 5.93–97.

mantras.anvaya: अब्धिजाताः समस्ताः रत्नजातयः च निशुम्भस्य (सन्ति); वह्निः अपि तुभ्यम् अग्निशौचे वाससी च ददौ।
mantras.anvaya_en: A nominal sentence of possession (genitive निशुम्भस्य with the copula understood), then a finite clause with ददौ and its dative and object.
mantras.lit: And all the kinds of jewels born of the ocean are Niśumbha’s; Fire too gave you a pair of garments purified by fire.
mantras.tr: ‘Every kind of gem the ocean yields belongs to Niśumbha; and even Agni has given you two garments purified by fire.’

comm.t: The catalogue ends with the ocean’s gems, held by Niśumbha, and Agni’s gift of fire-cleansed garments to Śumbha. Like the Ocean in 5.96, Agni gives: the conquered gods now serve. In the digital text a footnote asterisk of the printed book followed वह्निरपि; it has been removed (corrections.json, encoding).
Agni’s office (वह्निकर्म, 5.4) was among those the brothers seized. Garments ‘purified by fire’ are traditionally understood as cloth that fire cleanses without burning.

mantras.anvaya: दैत्येन्द्र, एवं समस्तानि रत्नानि ते आहृतानि; एषा कल्याणी स्त्रीरत्नं त्वया कस्मात् न गृह्यते?
mantras.anvaya_en: A summary statement (रत्नानि … आहृतानि) and a rhetorical question in the passive (एषा … कस्मात् न गृह्यते).
mantras.lit: Thus, O lord of the daityas, all the jewels have been brought to you; why is this lovely one, a jewel among women, not taken by you?
mantras.tr: ‘So, lord of the demons, every treasure has been brought to you. Why then do you not take this lovely one, the jewel among women?’

comm.t: The servants close their report with its conclusion: every ratna is already Śumbha’s, so the one ratna still missing, the Goddess, should be taken too. The speech that began in 5.90 ends here.
A modern reading: the argument from possession is the demons’ undoing. Having taken everything, they assume the Goddess can be taken like the rest.

samasa.sense: the two servants who made the report

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (ग्रीवा shortened to -ग्रीव at the end)
samasa.sense: a proper name: the demon messenger (not the monkey-king of the Rāmāyaṇa)

morph.note: Periphrastic perfect of the causative stem प्रेषय- (प्र + √इष्, ‘send’): stem + -आम् + the perfect of √अस् (आस). Derived stems form their perfect this way.
Absolutive with a prefix, so -ya (lyap) instead of -tvā: ‘having heard’. नि + √शम्, as in निशामय (1.2).
Genitive with दूतम्: the person to whom a messenger is sent may be put in the genitive (‘messenger to the Devī’).

mantras.anvaya: चण्डमुण्डयोः इति वचः निशम्य सः शुम्भः तदा महासुरं सुग्रीवं देव्याः दूतं प्रेषयामास।
mantras.anvaya_en: An absolutive clause (निशम्य … वचः), then subject (शुम्भः, resumed by सः), verb प्रेषयामास, and object सुग्रीवम् with the predicate दूतम्.
mantras.lit: Having heard these words of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, Śumbha then sent the great asura Sugrīva as messenger to the Devī.
mantras.tr: Hearing what Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa said, Śumbha sent the mighty demon Sugrīva as his envoy to the Goddess.

comm.t: Śumbha acts at once on the report: he does not go to see her, as the servants urged (5.92), but sends an envoy, the asura Sugrīva. His instructions follow in 5.103.

The embassy gives the chapter its name in the colophon, देव्या दूतसंवादः ‘the Goddess’s dialogue with the messenger’. Sugrīva the demon is a different figure from the monkey-king of the Rāmāyaṇa who bears the same name.
